summary: 100-foot Aermotor tower in Sawyer County, WI; DNR planned to end its fire use in 2016; county expressed interest in two towers; NHLR-registered 2017.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with a US Forest Service-style stairway
facts.status_note: Listed as standing by firelookout.org; the DNR planned to take its fire towers out of service in 2016, and no source read confirms its condition after that

access.note: County article (written after the DNR decommissioned its towers) says the two tower sites it discussed are secured with fences and locks; it is not confirmed that either is the Hayward tower. No current access source found.

events.note: Tower survey dated 1940 shows a wooden stairway style tower in place; the sources do not say whether it was this tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The earlier Sawyer County Record article places the Hayward tower south of Hayward; the county article describes an unnamed county-leased tower off Highway B four miles east of Hayward. Not confirmed to be the same tower; the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Build date is unknown per NHLR, so no built event. Status 'standing' rests on the firelookout.org listing; the NHLR page does not state status. The county article prints no year; it describes the towers after the DNR decommissioned them. Its 'off Highway B four miles east of Hayward' tower is matched to Hayward only by inference, so access stays 'unknown', which matches the tower record; the fenced-and-locked description may not apply to Hayward. Staffing and fire history for this tower not found. The 60-towers-manned figure is a statewide quote from DNR's Trent Marty in the Sawyer County Record article [2], not a Hayward-specific fact. Search results included a Wisconsin Historical Society record for the 1928 DNR ranger station, which is a different building and was not used.
